name: mcp-scanner-893327c5-blind30-ots
instr:
# mcp-scanner-regen

Someone points this software at a running server, at a published bundle of code, or at a directory of source, expects back the operations that server offers together with warnings about them, and now gets wrong answers in a great many places. Nothing about the servers being looked at changed, and nothing about how the software is driven changed. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

Getting hold of the thing to be examined already goes wrong. With a private index address set, the hosts permitted for downloading a distribution come back nearly bare — that index's own host and the usual public download and metadata hosts all missing — while the narrower set permitted for metadata alone still lists the index host as it should. Unpacking a source distribution that arrives as a .zip into a destination directory now fails instead of handing back the root of the tree it wrote, so a file that should sit directly under that root cannot be read. Pointing it at a directory of source finds nothing to read: asking for the sources ending in .py beneath a directory yields no files whatsoever, even when one sits directly in it beside an unrelated .txt. The whole-bundle sweep for sources ending in .ts opens nothing either, and stays quiet about it — even when every single file blows up on being read in, no failure is recorded, so the run comes back with nothing to report and no errors, indistinguishable from a bundle swept end to end and found clean
